Pipeline / Outbound stage conversion

Positive-reply-to-meeting booking rate

The percentage of positive-intent prospects booking a valid meeting within the agreed follow-up window. This explicitly measures progression from the prior positive-response stage rather than from all contacted leads.

Explore in the metric hierarchy ↗Open calculators →
Level 4Inspect the detail

The percentage of positive-intent prospects booking a valid meeting within the agreed follow-up window. This explicitly measures progression from the prior positive-response stage rather than from all contacted leads.

%

How we use it

We assess scheduling friction, response ownership, and the clarity of the proposed next step.

Transparent calculationUnique positive-intent prospects with a valid meeting booked / unique positive-intent prospects in the same matured cohort * 100
positive prospects with booking36
positive intent prospects90

36 / 90 * 100 = 40% booking conversion from positive replies.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Owner and follow-up speed
  • Meeting type and market
  • Persona and outreach source

Questions we investigate

  • Where do interested prospects stop before booking?
  • Are calendar availability and time zones causing friction?
  • Do repeat bookings inflate the numerator?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Clarify the meeting value and next step.
  • Improve routing and calendar availability.
  • Compare booked and held meetings separately.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Sales development lead
Weekly for cohorts with a complete booking window.

Required data

  • Positive-response cohort membership
  • Deduplicated booking records and prospect IDs
  • Booking window and validity rules

Read the measure with context

Zero positive-intent prospects makes the rate undefined. Deduplicate reschedules and multiple invitations. Booked, held, and qualified meetings are separate outcomes; immature cohorts can understate eventual bookings.
